# The model layers

<!-- purpose: Which layer of the model holds what, and the directory its files live in -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

A SWCraft model is a directory of YAML files: one file per element, its file name derived from the element's own identity and identical to it unless another element's file already holds that name. Each layer below is one directory, and each page lists every kind of element that layer holds and every key those elements accept.

| Layer | What it holds | Where the files live |
|---|---|---|
| [Requirements](requirements.md) | Requirements and specification items, identified by `id` rather than `name`; the architecture elements that realize one name it in their own `satisfies`. An architecture requirement is published in the generated `needs.json` as a need of its own; an imported one is never published, only named by its id in the links that reach it. | `requirements/` |
| [Compositions](compositions.md) | Composition types, one file each: the structural hierarchy of the architecture. A composition declares boundary ports of its own, holds named members that instantiate declared component and composition types, and delegates its ports to its members'. The hierarchy is by reference exactly as AUTOSAR spells it — a member names a type rather than nesting it — so the directory stays flat however deep the instantiation goes. | `compositions/` |
| [SWCs](swc.md) | Software components, one file each under `swc/{group}/`; the group is the file's directory, not a key inside the file. | `swc/` |
| [Interfaces](interfaces.md) | Port interfaces. Three element kinds discriminated by `kind`: `sender_receiver` (typed data elements), `client_server` (operations with typed, directional arguments) and `external_interface` (a stub for an interface declared outside the project, carrying the reference the source made to it). | `interfaces/` |
| [Application Types](application_types.md) | Application data types, one file each under `data_types/application/`: the physical view of the data a model exchanges. Four element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`enum`, `record`, `array`, `application_type`), plus four nested member kinds (`enum_literal`, `record_field`, `conversion`, `range`). A record field and an array element name an application type; a data element and an argument name one by their `application_type`, and a mapping set pairs one with the implementation type that stores it. An application type and an implementation type may carry one name. The directory is mandatory and may be empty. | `data_types/application/` |
| [Implementation Types](implementation_types.md) | Implementation data types, one file each under `data_types/implementation/`: how the platform stores the data a model exchanges. Six element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`value_type`, `reference_type`, `external_type`, `implementation_record`, `implementation_array`, `pointer`), plus one nested member kind (`implementation_element`). A `value_type` is the implementation type that rests on a base type, an element of the `base_types` layer, a `reference_type` rests on another implementation type, and `implementation_record`, `implementation_array` and `pointer` are the implementation structure, array and pointer; a mapping set pairs each application type, an element of the `application_types` layer, with the implementation type that stores it. An `external_type` is a stub for an implementation type declared outside the project. An implementation type and an application type may carry one name. The directory is mandatory and may be empty. | `data_types/implementation/` |
| [Base Types](base_types.md) | Base types, one file each under `data_types/base/`: how the platform stores a value — its size, its encoding and its C declaration. One kind, `base_type`, which a `value_type` names as its `base` and which no data element, argument, record field or array element names. The directory is mandatory and may be empty. | `data_types/base/` |
| [Units](units.md) | Units, one file each under `data_types/units/`: the unit a physical value is measured in, an element a type names by reference. One kind, `unit`, which an application type names as its `unit_ref` and a `linear` compu method as its `unit`. The directory is mandatory and may be empty. | `data_types/units/` |
| [Compu Methods](compu_methods.md) | Computation methods, one file each under `data_types/compu_methods/`: how a stored value becomes the physical or the named one, an element a type names by reference. Two element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`texttable`, `linear`), plus one nested member kind (`table_entry`). An enumeration, a value type and a reference type name a `texttable` by their `compu_method_ref`, an application type names a `linear` by its own. The directory is mandatory and may be empty. | `data_types/compu_methods/` |
| [Data Constraints](data_constraints.md) | Data constraints, one file each under `data_types/constraints/`: the physical limits a value is declared within, an element a type names by reference. One kind, `data_constr`, which an application type names as its `data_constr_ref`. The directory is mandatory and may be empty. | `data_types/constraints/` |
| [Mapping Sets](mapping_sets.md) | Data type mapping sets, one file each under `data_types/mapping_sets/`. A set pairs each application type — the physical view of a signal, with its unit, its conversion and its range — with the implementation type that stores it, and a component names the sets its behaviour maps with. Every application type or enumeration a component's ports speak in has to be paired in one of them, because generated code needs to know what stores it. The directory is mandatory and may be empty: a project whose interfaces are typed by implementation types alone needs no set. | `data_types/mapping_sets/` |
| [Connectors](connectors.md) | Assembly connectors, each joining one component's `provide` port to another component's `require` port over a compatible interface. | `connectors/` |
| [Tasks](tasks.md) | OS tasks and the runnables each one executes. `period` is in seconds; a budget, `wcet`, carries its own unit. | `tasks/` |
| [Sequences](sequences.md) | Sequence scenarios, one task each; each is drawn as a sequence diagram whose files are named from the scenario's name. | `sequences/` |
| [Hardware](hardware.md) | The processor the software runs on, its cores, the partitions its tasks run in, and the memories those cores may use. Exactly one processor is declared; every task runs in a declared partition on a declared core, and every memory a component budgets is declared here. | `hardware/` |
